## Claims
- [source-backed] RWY Theorem 4.8 integrally generates \(J_v\subseteq\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by the right- and lower-adjoined Schur families, with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]
- [source-backed] St. Dizier–Yong prove that the lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) minimally generates \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- [proved] For \((n,r,s,t)=(8,4,4,3)\), the source parameters are \(i=j=a=b=2\). Hence the cited theorem concerns \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{4,8})\cong\Lambda/I_{4,4}\) and the six lower-adjoined classes indexed by \(22\subseteq\mu\subseteq(22,2^2)\).
- [source-backed] The 2024 paper’s Algorithm 1 is a terminating coproduct-tensor reduction for its tall/wide LR-equation system, with input a valid tuple and a tall partition; it is not presented as a degreewise Pieri-matrix block algorithm. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 494-516; 598-610; 743-775]

## Strategy
Compared the two inspected full-text works at the specialization \(i=j=n-r=r-j=2\). The 2024 result supplies lower-family minimality, while its algorithm acts on Hopf-algebra tensors and LR linear forms rather than constructing sparse degreewise Pieri blocks, selected rows, or unimodular/SNF certificates.

## Gaps
The requested target—derive and test a sparse, degreewise block algorithm for the \((2,2,4,4)\) Pieri matrices—was **not established** by the inspected literature. No inspected source supplies that algorithm or its case-specific matrix certificates. This is a bounded negative result only for RWY (2011) and St. Dizier–Yong (2024).

## Next
A direct construction and finite exact verification of the requested Pieri blocks remains necessary.
